packageRules.description: react-router, react-start and router-devtools bump together. react-start adds the `server` route option to react-router's types by declaration merging across package boundaries, and the two ship on separate version lines, so they can drift. When they do, the lockfile holds the pinned react-router while react-start's transitive requirement pulls a second, newer router-core: the augmentation merges into one copy and the route files resolve the other, and every server route stops typechecking with 'server does not exist'. The code is correct throughout, which is what makes it expensive to diagnose. Scoped to the coupled packages on purpose — react-table and the standalone devtools are independent and keep their own PRs.
